protocol: CoAP (RFC 7252) — CON GET request + piggybacked ACK 2.05 Content response, over UDP/5683. Extensions exercised: RFC 9175 Echo option (252), OCF vendor option 2049.

Everything structural is canonical: options are in ascending option-number order; the 12-byte Uri-Query uses a direct length nibble because only 13/14/15 are reserved as escapes; the 26-byte Uri-Query uses lenNib=13 with ext=26-13=13; Echo (252) after Accept (17) forces delta 235, i.e. deltaNib=13 with ext=235-13=222. The running option number is 0,11,11,15,15,17,252 — option 6's identity is NOT derivable without having decoded options 1..5.

Note the canonical-form trap baked in here: Content-Format 50 encodes as ONE byte 0x32 and Max-Age 60 as ONE byte 0x3c, because CoAP uint options are minimum-length. Content-Format 0 (text/plain) would encode as a ZERO-byte value (lenNib=0), and Max-Age 65536 as three bytes. Option value width is a function of the value, not of the option.

captures.notes: Constructed, not captured — option 2049 is a real OCF/IoTivity vendor option but pairing it with a bare Uri-Path is my choice to force the 14-escape in the smallest possible packet. It is legal CoAP. Registered IANA options rarely produce a delta >= 269 in one hop, so this escape is exercised in practice mainly by vendor/experimental option numbers and by >=269-byte option values (e.g. a long Proxy-Uri, which uses the identical 14-escape on the LENGTH nibble — structurally the same construct, so I did not emit a third 269-byte capture for it). Note also: tkl=0 means the token field has length zero, which is NOT the same as tkl=1 with value 0x00.

statefulness:
CoAP's state is a poor fit for §5 in a way that is structural, not cosmetic: §5 models a CONNECTION (disconnected -> connected -> authenticated) and hangs `validIn`/`requires`/`conflicts`/`expires` off it. CoAP over UDP has no connection and no session. Its state is (a) per-message-ID transaction state and (b) per-token exchange state, and those two live at different layers with different lifetimes. Everything below is what this protocol actually demands.

LEGAL-MESSAGE-PER-STATE. There is no "logged in" gate; every request is legal at any time. What IS state-gated is the message TYPE. An ACK (T=2) is legal only while an inbound CON with that exact MID is unacknowledged, and exactly once — a second ACK for the same MID is a protocol error, not a retransmit. RST (T=3) is legal at any time and unilaterally kills the exchange. An empty message (code 0.00) is legal only with tkl=0 AND zero options AND no payload — an intra-message cross-field validity rule §5 cannot state at all (`validIn` gates messages by session state, never fields by each other). An empty CON is a ping and its only legal answer is an RST.

MUST CHAIN. (1) MID: a CON creates an obligation to receive an ACK/RST with the same MID within EXCHANGE_LIFETIME; the retransmission schedule (ACK_TIMEOUT 2 s x ACK_RANDOM_FACTOR 1.5, doubling, MAX_RETRANSMIT 4) is mandated, and §4's `loop:{max:n}` with a constant bound plus an `on:"timeout"` edge can express the COUNT but not the randomised exponential backoff — there is no per-attempt timeout expression. (2) TOKEN: a request creates an obligation to receive a response bearing the same token, and this outlives the MID exchange. (3) Blockwise (RFC 7959): a 2.05 carrying Block2 with M=1 mandates a further GET with NUM+1 and the same token until M=0, a chain whose length is unknown when the first request is sent — §4's rule that a back edge must carry a CONSTANT `loop:{max:n}` means blockwise is expressible only by picking an arbitrary cap. (4) Echo (RFC 9175): a 4.01 carrying Echo mandates re-sending the SAME request with that Echo option copied in — chaining triggered by a decoded option, which `implies` handles well.

MUST NEVER COMBINE. Proxy-Uri MUST NOT appear with Uri-Host/Uri-Port/Uri-Path/Uri-Query. This is FIELD-level mutual exclusion within one message; §5's `conflicts` is MESSAGE-level within a session and cannot express it. Similarly Block1 and Block2 in a single request mean different things and Observe MUST NOT appear on anything but GET/FETCH.

CONFIRMED vs PRESUMED — and CoAP is unusually explicit about it. A 2.05 response is CONFIRMED for exactly Max-Age seconds (capture 2, byte 16 = 60 s) and PRESUMED thereafter. That maps onto §5's `confidence`/`ttl` almost perfectly — except `ttl` is shown as a literal "PT30S" and here it must come from the wire (`"ttl":"capture.maxAge | seconds"`). A 2.03 Valid response is the case §5 has no primitive for: it revalidates an existing fact via ETag WITHOUT restating its value, so it must REFRESH the TTL of a fact it does not carry. An ACK for a PUT/POST confirms the message ARRIVED; it does not confirm the effect, which stays presumed until an observation — exactly §5's setRelay/getRelay pattern, and the one place §5 fits CoAP cleanly.

DISCOVERED-WRONG-FROM-THE-NEXT-RESPONSE. Four distinct cases, and they are the norm rather than the exception here. (1) An EMPTY ACK (code 0.00) means "received, response later" — you only learn from the ACK itself that this exchange is separate rather than piggybacked, and you must then keep the token alive and wait for a fresh CON you will have to ACK. That is a state transition driven by a decoded field and `implies` handles it: {"when":"capture.code == 0x00","state":"awaitingSeparateResponse"}. (2) 4.02 Bad Option means the server did not understand a CRITICAL option you presumed it supported — a capability you assumed, refuted one round-trip late. (3) 4.01 + Echo means your request's freshness was rejected; you learn the server's anti-replay state only by being refused. (4) RST means the peer has no record of the exchange — for an Observe registration this silently invalidates a relationship you have been presuming for hours.

NEGOTIATED CAPABILITY — §5 names this as a known gap and CoAP confirms it hard. You send Observe:0; the server may answer WITHOUT the Observe option, which means "declined, here is a one-shot response". The response grants LESS than requested and the difference is signalled by an ABSENCE. Nothing in §5 lets a message declare "what I asked for is X, what I got is Y, bind Y". Same shape for Block2: you propose SZX=6 (1024 B), the server may answer SZX=4 (256 B), and every subsequent request in the chain must adopt the server's smaller size.

SEQUENCE NUMBERS / DEDUP — also on §5's gap list, also confirmed. Two independent counters. (a) Message ID: a server MUST keep a dedup window of recently-seen MIDs for EXCHANGE_LIFETIME (247 s) and re-send the SAME cached ACK for a retransmitted non-idempotent request rather than re-executing it. §5 has an `idempotent:true` flag but no window primitive to make it mean anything. (b) Observe: the option value is a 24-bit counter that WRAPS, with a reordering rule (accept only if V1 < V2 < V1+2^23, or the notification is older than 128 s) — a sliding window with a time component that has no expression in §6 either. MID also carries a lease obligation the grammar cannot state: a token MUST NOT be reused while an old exchange could still deliver a late response bound to it (the reason RFC 9175 Request-Tag exists). §6's `seq.next` gives a monotonic counter, which covers MID generation and nothing else.

FRAGMENTATION — no reassembly primitive, confirmed by blockwise above.

MODAL/EXCLUSIVE STATE — the one §5 gap this protocol does NOT exercise. CoAP has no firmware-update-style mode; a resource going 5.03 Service Unavailable with Max-Age is the closest analogue and is per-resource, not per-device.

gaps.what: Decoder-carried accumulator: the option number is a running SUM of every preceding option's delta, so decoding option N requires state produced by options 0..N-1. `each` in v0 is a pure per-item map with no fold variable, no `prev`, no `index`, and no field-level `compute`.
gaps.why: Capture 1 byte 71-72: `d8 de`. dNib=13 -> extended -> delta = 0xde + 13 = 235. The option's identity is 235 + (11+0+4+0+2) = 252 (Echo). The bytes `d8 de` carry NO absolute option number; the value 17 that must be added to them exists only as the accumulated result of decoding bytes 8, 16, 28, 41, 69. Decode is not a pure per-field fold. Symmetrically on encode: emitting the Echo option's nibble requires knowing that the last option emitted was 17.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a fold binding to `each`, making it a fold rather than a map, in BOTH modes:
{ "each":"inputs.options", "as":"o",
  "fold":{ "var":"prev", "init":"0", "next":"o.number" },
  "fields":[ ... uses `prev` ... ] }
and in decode:
{ "each":{...}, "as":"options",
  "fold":{ "var":"num", "init":"0", "next":"num + item.delta" },
  "fields":[ ..., { "let":"number", "value":"num + item.delta" } ] }
`fold.var` is read-only inside the iteration and advances after it. Cyclic/self-referential folds are a validate-time error, same rule as span cycles. This single primitive also covers DNS name-compression offsets, running checksums and frame counters.

gaps.what: No variable-length opaque field in DECODE mode. There is no way to read N bytes where N is an expression.
gaps.why: Three separate places in one packet. (a) Capture 1 bytes 4-7: the token is `tkl` bytes and tkl is a NIBBLE from byte 0. (b) Every option value: bytes 9-15 is 7 bytes, bytes 43-68 is 26 bytes derived from lNib=13 plus ext byte 0x0d. (c) Capture 2 bytes 18-41: the payload. v0 offers `skip:n` (fixed, and it DISCARDS the bytes — useless for a token that must be echoed for correlation), fixed-width scalars, and `each` over a count (yields List<Int>, not Bytes). `slice`/`take`/`drop` are converters over a value already in hand, not readers over the stream.

gaps.what: `each` in decode cannot be terminated by a sentinel or by end-of-input. It takes only a count expression, and the option-list length is not knowable without decoding the options.
gaps.why: Capture 1: the option list runs from byte 8 to byte 80 and ends at the END OF THE DATAGRAM with no sentinel byte whatsoever. Capture 2: the list runs bytes 8..16 and ends at the 0xff marker at byte 17 — but 0xff is also a legal byte INSIDE an option value, so the terminator is only recognisable at an option boundary. There is no expression that can be placed in `each`'s count slot in either case; the count is a RESULT of the parse.

gaps.what: `bits` has no decode form. Its entries are defined as {n, value}; there is no {n, as}.
gaps.why: Capture 1 byte 0 = 0x44 is ver(2b)=1 | type(2b)=0 | tkl(4b)=4, and byte 8 = 0xb7 is deltaNib(4b) | lenNib(4b). Both must be read to parse anything at all. §3 says decode fields 'carry as: instead of a value', but gives no example for `bits`, and the decode example uses only whole scalars. Every CoAP field in the first byte and in every option header is unreadable.

gaps.what: No conditional in the expression language, so a value that is a function of a threshold cannot be computed. Specifically the delta and length NIBBLES.
gaps.why: lenNib = len<13 ? len : (len<269 ? 13 : 14). Capture 1 byte 28 is 0x4c (len 12, DIRECT) and byte 41 is 0x0d (len 26, ESCAPE) — the same source expression `len(value)` must produce 12 in one case and 13 in the other. `when` cannot rescue this: `when` selects whole FIELDS, and both nibbles are emitted by ONE `bits` field occupying ONE byte. You cannot conditionally emit half a byte. The converter table has no arithmetic or comparison converters at all (only `len`), though §3/§6 examples do use infix `/` and `==`, so the expression language is larger than the table admits — that under-specification is itself a finding.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a ternary function to the expression language and document the full infix operator set (+ - * / % == != < <= > >= && || ! and, for CoAP response codes, >> &):
  "value": "if(d < 13, d, if(d < 269, 13, 14))"
Smallest possible generalising fix — one function, no new field kind, no engine change beyond the evaluator. Alternatively a `bucket(v, [13,269], [13,14])` converter, but `if()` is more useful everywhere else.

gaps.what: No record/struct type in `inputs`, so a list of (optionNumber, value) pairs cannot be supplied. `type` is scalars plus `list<T-scalar>`.
gaps.why: A CoAP option set IS a list of pairs: [(11,"sensors"),(11,"temperature"),(15,"unit=celsius"),(15,"since=..."),(17,0x32),(252,0xa1b2...)]. With only list<text> you can model repeated Uri-Path via `inputs.uri | split('/')`, but you cannot model a heterogeneous option set, and the first segment still needs delta 11 while the rest need delta 0 (see gap 1). Consequence: the encode document I wrote must hard-code one option group per option, in one fixed order — packet replay, not a protocol description. Adding `when` to any non-final option corrupts every later delta.
gaps.proposedFix:
Extend the input type system with a record and a list of records:
{ "name":"options", "kind":"internal", "type":"list<record>",
  "record":{ "number":"u16", "value":"bytes" } }
Field access inside `each` is `o.number` / `o.value`. Symmetrically, `each` in decode gains "yields":"record" so it produces a list of records rather than a list of scalars. Without this, no TLV-shaped protocol (CoAP, SNMP varbinds, BER, DHCP options) is expressible generally.

gaps.what: No minimum-length unsigned integer encoding. CoAP uint option values are variable-width with no leading zeros; a value of 0 is a ZERO-BYTE value.
gaps.why: Capture 2 byte 14: Content-Format 50 -> `32` (1 byte). Byte 16: Max-Age 60 -> `3c` (1 byte). But Content-Format 0 (text/plain) -> ZERO bytes with lenNib=0; Max-Age 90000 -> 3 bytes `01 5f 90`; Accept 11543 -> 2 bytes. v0's scalars are all fixed-width, so `{"u8":"inputs.maxAge"}` emits `00` for 0 (illegal — CoAP mandates the empty encoding) and truncates above 255. This also breaks the LENGTH nibble, which must equal the width the value happens to need.
gaps.proposedFix:
Two converters:
  `minuint`   Int -> Bytes, big-endian, leading zero bytes stripped, 0 -> empty
  `unminuint` Bytes -> Int, empty -> 0
Used as { "bytes":{ "value":"inputs.maxAge | minuint" } } and { "n":4, "value":"inputs.maxAge | minuint | len" }. Cheapest fix in the whole list, and it also serves BER/DER, SNMP, and DNS TTL-style encodings. Round-trip is exact because CoAP itself forbids the non-minimal form.

gaps.what: No `remaining` / frame-length path. The payload runs to the end of the UDP datagram; its length is carried by the transport, not by any field in the message.
gaps.why: Capture 2 bytes 18..41: nothing in the message says '24'. The only source of that number is the UDP datagram length. §2's `frame` kinds are lengthPrefixed | delimited | fixed | none — all STREAM framings; `none` under `udp` presumably means one datagram per message but exposes no length, and §6's path list has no `remaining`, `frame.length` or `eof`.
gaps.proposedFix: Add `frame.length`, `frame.offset`, `remaining` (= frame.length - frame.offset) and boolean `eof` to the §6 path set, defined for every layer that has a determinate frame boundary (udp datagram, lengthPrefixed/fixed/delimited stream frames). Then { "bytes":{"len":"remaining"}, "as":"payload" } works. Encode-side `remaining` is undefined and must be a validate-time error.

gaps.what: No per-iteration capture scope in `each` during decode. A `when` inside an iteration cannot reliably refer to a field decoded earlier in the SAME iteration.
gaps.why: Capture 1 byte 71 = 0xd8: whether byte 72 exists at all depends on dNib==13, decoded from the high nibble of byte 71 one field earlier and one iteration among six. Writing "when":"capture.dNib == 13" is ambiguous — v0's only `each` decode example emits a flat List of scalars under a single outer `as`, and never defines what `capture.<x>` means for a field inside an iteration. Get this wrong and iteration 6 reads iteration 3's dNib.
gaps.proposedFix: Define a scoped binding: inside `each`, fields written with `as` land on `item.*` for the current iteration and are also collected into the outer list; `capture.*` continues to mean message scope. Add a `let` pseudo-field for derived per-iteration values that consume no bytes: { "let":"delta", "value":"if(item.dNib<13, item.dNib, ...)" }. This is the decode-side counterpart of gap 6 and should ship with it.

gaps.what: The `coap` sugar layer is listed in §2 but has NO declared parameter schema anywhere in the spec, and using it is precisely the protocol-specific code path §7 forbids.
gaps.why: §2 lists `coap` as sugar that 'expands to bytes + a transport intent'. §7 says 'If any of the three needs a code path specific to that protocol, the grammar has failed'. Since gaps 1-6 make the `bytes` layer unable to express CoAP, the sugar layer is not a convenience — it is the ONLY way CoAP works, and it is a hand-written CoAP codec inside the engine. Worse, a user-authored or ai-draft document cannot see inside it: there is no stated way to add an unregistered option (2049 in capture 3), to control non-canonical encodings, or to decode a message the sugar does not model.
gaps.proposedFix: Two things. (1) Publish the layer's parameter schema so a document can actually use it and a validator can type-check it: { "kind":"coap", "type":"con|non|ack|rst", "code":"0.01", "messageId":"seq.next", "token":"inputs.token", "options":"inputs.options", "payload":"inputs.body" } with options as list<record>{number,value} so unregistered numbers work. (2) Require every sugar layer to be DEFINED as a bytes-layer macro in the grammar itself and to be dumpable (`expand`), so 'sugar compiles to bytes' is a checkable claim rather than an assertion. If gaps 1-6 land, that macro is writable — I have written it at the foot of the encode document.

gaps.what: `expect` correlation cannot express CoAP's two-tier matching (message-id AND token, at different times), nor the piggybacked-vs-separate response branch.
gaps.why: §4 offers socket | token | broadcast. CoAP needs BOTH keys simultaneously: the ACK at capture-2 bytes 2-3 correlates on messageId 0x1234, while the RESPONSE correlates on token 9af31c08 at bytes 4-7. In a piggybacked exchange one datagram satisfies both. In a SEPARATE exchange the server sends an empty ACK (code 0.00, tkl=0 — so it carries NO token to correlate on) and the real 2.05 arrives later as a fresh CON with a DIFFERENT message id and the original token, which the client must then ACK. `token` correlation alone cannot match the empty ACK; `socket` correlation is meaningless on UDP.

gaps.what: State model: no message-id dedup window and no retransmission schedule primitive. §5 has an `idempotent` flag with nothing to attach it to.
gaps.why: A CON must be retransmitted at ACK_TIMEOUT 2 s x ACK_RANDOM_FACTOR 1.5, doubling, MAX_RETRANSMIT 4 — randomised exponential backoff. §4 can express the retry COUNT via a back edge with loop:{max:4} and an on:"timeout" edge, but there is no per-attempt timeout expression and no jitter. On the receive side, a server MUST cache the ACK it sent for a given messageId for EXCHANGE_LIFETIME (247 s) and replay it verbatim for a duplicate, never re-executing a non-idempotent request. Capture 1's MID 0x1234 is the dedup key and nothing in §5 can name it.

gaps.what: State model: no negotiated-capability primitive. A CoAP response can grant less than requested, and the refusal is signalled by an ABSENCE.
gaps.why: Send Observe:0 (option 6) in a GET; a server that declines answers 2.05 with NO Observe option at all. The client must bind 'not observing' from a missing field. Same for Block2: propose SZX=6 (1024 B), the server may answer SZX=4 (256 B) and every subsequent request must adopt the server's value. §5 has `requires`/`validIn`/`effects` but no way to say 'I asked for X, bind what was actually granted, and gate later messages on that'. §5 lists this gap for MQTT SUBACK; CoAP confirms it independently and adds the harder absence-signalled variant.
gaps.proposedFix:
"negotiates": { "requested":"inputs.observe",
                "granted":"capture.options | option(6) | unminuint",
                "absentMeans":"denied",
                "bindTo":"session.observing" }
plus `validIn` accepting an expression over session.* so later messages can gate on the granted value. `absentMeans` is the key addition — negotiation by omission is common (CoAP Observe, HTTP content negotiation, TLS extensions).

gaps.what: No field-level mutual exclusion. §5's `conflicts` is message-scoped within a session; CoAP needs option-scoped exclusion within a single message.
gaps.why: Proxy-Uri (35) MUST NOT appear together with Uri-Host (3), Uri-Port (7), Uri-Path (11) or Uri-Query (15) in the same message. Capture 1 carries Uri-Path and Uri-Query; adding a Proxy-Uri makes it malformed, and no v0 construct can say so. Likewise an empty message (code 0.00) MUST have tkl=0 and zero options — a cross-field constraint inside one message.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add message-level assertions evaluated at validate time where inputs are static and at encode time otherwise:
"invariants": [
  { "exclusive": [["proxyUri"],["uriHost","uriPort","uriPath","uriQuery"]],
    "message":"Proxy-Uri cannot combine with Uri-* options" },
  { "when":"inputs.code == 0", "require":"len(inputs.token)==0 && len(inputs.options)==0" } ]

gaps.what: No ordering guarantee or assertion on an encoded list. An out-of-order option list silently produces a corrupt packet with a wrapped negative delta.
gaps.why: Options must be emitted in ascending option-number order because the delta is unsigned. Given [(17,...),(11,...)] the delta for the second is 11-17 = -6, which packs into a 4-bit nibble as 10 — the encoder emits a syntactically valid but semantically wrong packet (option 27, Block1) with no error. v0 has neither a sort nor an assert field.

gaps.what: `effects.ttl` is a literal ISO-8601 duration; the authoritative TTL arrives on the wire.
gaps.why: Capture 2 byte 16 is Max-Age = 60, which is exactly how long the decoded temperature fact is CONFIRMED before it degrades to presumed. §5's example hard-codes "ttl":"PT30S". Related: a 2.03 Valid response refreshes an existing fact's TTL by ETag WITHOUT restating the value, and §5 has no 'revalidate without value' operation.
gaps.proposedFix: Let `ttl` accept an expression: "ttl":"capture.maxAge | seconds" (add a `seconds`/`duration` converter, Int -> Duration). Add an effect verb for revalidation: "effects":{ "revalidate":{ "fact":"dev.sensor.temp", "matchEtag":"capture.etag", "ttl":"capture.maxAge | seconds" } }.

gaps.what: Round-trip is not exact in two places, both genuinely ambiguous rather than merely unimplemented.
gaps.why: (a) Empty payload vs no payload: 0xff MUST be omitted when the payload is empty, so encode(payload="") and encode(no payload) both produce capture-2-minus-bytes-17..41 — decode cannot distinguish them and decode(encode(x)) loses the distinction. (b) The `code` byte is class(3b).detail(5b); decoded as a u8 it round-trips exactly, but any expression over it (§5's example "capture.status == 401") needs `capture.code >> 5 == 4`, and §6 documents no bitwise operators. Everything ELSE about CoAP is canonically unique and round-trips exactly: the 13/14 escape choice is forced by magnitude (13 and 268 both take the 8-bit form, 269 forces the 16-bit form with ext=0), option order is fixed by the ascending rule, and repeated-option order is semantically meaningful and preserved. That is worth stating plainly — the framing hazards here are real but the encoding itself is not ambiguous.
gaps.proposedFix: (a) Have decode set a distinct boolean capture rather than an empty value: { "u8":null, "as":"payloadMarker", "when":"!eof" } with `capture.hasPayload` = presence of the marker, and require encode to derive the marker from `hasPayload` not from `len(payload) > 0`. (b) Document the full operator set including >> << & | ^, or decode `code` with the extended `bits` from gap 4: { "bits":[{"n":3,"as":"codeClass"},{"n":5,"as":"codeDetail"}] }.
